title: Bix and Trumbauer join Whiteman; the Washboard Blues record and Changes
summary: Bix and Trumbauer joined in Indianapolis; Challis added a small jazz group to the Hoagy record and used all the singers on Changes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, you can get awfully sick, if you're in the band, you got to play that stuff, especially when you got some guys that love to improvise, like Jimmy and Tommy and Steve and well, let's see, at that time Trumbauer and Bix had joined, they joined in Indianapolis.
Yeah, they came in because they weren't doing -- the band wasn't doing so hot, they had a lot of time on their hands. So they joined the band in Indianapolis, Steve had joined it before that.

So I just figured I'd get a little jazz band in there somewhere on the record, so I had Jimmy, Tommy and I didn't have a piano -- Jimmy, Tommy and Steve and Bix and they played the part. They just played just a chorus or so and then we went back to Hoagy's singing, and geez, it worked out well.
That was our record, and then they gave me a tune by the name of "Changes," a Walter Donaldson tune, awfully nice.

It turned out well. I used all the voices in there. I went to Paul and asked him, I said, 'What do I use or what don't I use?' 'Use whatever you want.' So boy I did. I had everybody and I had the 'sweet' trio, 'sweet' in quotes and that is Johnny Fulton, Skin Young and Charlie Gaylord and then I put let's see, I put Rinker in with them because he could sing a falsetto and I had Bing sing -- he sang the patter. That worked out great, and Steve, of course, spanked his bass on the Beiderbecke part of it, and the vocalists I used in back of Bix and that was like a first, you know.
